description: Showcase of strong saved model analyses. Movement: wh, A-movement, head movement (V2, VSO, inversion), scrambling, control and exceptional Case marking. Each case is an exact copy of a saved analysis that passes the invariant sweep, the contract warnings, the offline visual and camera audits and the right-to-left mirror check without an exception.

cases.description: German V2 question: was moves through the v phase edge to the prefield and finite T moves to C over a head-final TP.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/79-de-v2-wh, analysis 1 of 2. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/79-de-v2-wh.

derivationStages.stageRecord: On the ordinary reading, was asks for the thing purchased, and Maria denotes the purchaser. The participle gekauft supplies the lexical predicate. The finite perfect auxiliary hat is introduced as T, combining tense, agreement, and perfect interpretation without a separate Perf head. Active v introduces the external argument, and silent interrogative C will host the finite auxiliary. Projection labels throughout are inherited from heads under Bare Phrase Structure; they do not represent an independently supplied X-bar template.
derivationStages.statement: Select the lexical objects for the object-question reading.

derivationStages.stageRecord: First merge was with gekauft as its selected internal argument, assigning was the Theme role. Adjoin gestern to this verbal object, interpreting it as locating the purchase event on the preceding day. Merge active v above that predicate; v licenses accusative on was. Finally merge Maria at the edge of the v-domain as the Agent. The complement precedes the participle, and the verbal predicate precedes silent v, implementing the head-final lexical domain of this German clause.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the purchase event with Maria as its external argument.

values.pronunciation: The edge occurrence is pronounced; the thematic occurrence is silent.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Treating active v as a phase head, internally merge was from its already established complement position to an additional outer edge of the v-domain. This intermediate position keeps the object accessible for subsequent movement to C across the phase boundary. The new edge occurrence is pronounced at this stage, while its thematic occurrence becomes silent. Maria remains in the inner external-argument position, so the interrogative's passage through the edge does not change the Agent assignment.
derivationStages.statement: Move the object interrogative to the active v-phase edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge hat as T with the participial v-domain, establishing the perfect auxiliary's selection of the gekauft predicate. T agrees with Maria, the accessible external argument, and licenses nominative on it. Accusative was is already case-licensed and does not intervene as an active nominative goal. Hat realizes present tense and third-person singular agreement. This analysis does not impose an English-style subject EPP on German T: Maria remains at the v-edge rather than moving to a separate T-specifier. Before verb-second movement, the auxiliary occupies the right-hand T position.
derivationStages.statement: Merge the finite perfect auxiliary and license the subject.

values.pronunciation: The C occurrence is pronounced; the T occurrence is silent.

derivationStages.stageRecord: First merge silent interrogative C with the T-domain, establishing a root constituent question. Then internally merge the finite auxiliary from the T position shown in the preceding stage into C. The resulting complex C head contains pronounced hat and silent C; the lower auxiliary occurrence is now silent. This head movement derives the finite verb's position before Maria and gestern. The interrogative phrase has not yet moved to the prefield, so this stage is not the completed surface clause.
derivationStages.statement: Establish interrogative C and move the finite auxiliary into it.

values.pronunciation: Only the highest wh occurrence is pronounced.

values.interpretation: For which thing x did Maria purchase x yesterday?

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge was from the previously established outer v-edge to the edge of the C-domain, satisfying C's interrogative edge requirement. The new highest occurrence is pronounced; both lower occurrences are silent. The highest occurrence takes matrix interrogative scope and binds the Theme variable at the original object position. The completed structure therefore asks what Maria purchased yesterday. Its pronounced terminals are Was hat Maria gestern gekauft, with the finite auxiliary in C and exactly one interrogative phrase preceding it.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the object question by moving was into the prefield.

cases.description: Passive raising: two separate A-movements, to the embedded and then the matrix subject position, with copy pronunciation; passive Voice licenses the by-agent.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit a84ade3, spellout-v3-product-20261018/01-en-passive-raising, analysis 1 of 1. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/spellout-v3-product-20261018/runs/01-en-passive-raising.
cases.sentence: The letter seems to have been written by Mary.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the determiner The with letter to form the definite nominal object. Treat Mary as a lexical proper-name D object. The other objects remain separate. Projection labels identify the category inherited from the projecting head; they do not introduce independently stipulated phrase-structure templates. The supplied lexical forms distinguish finite seems, infinitival have, perfect-participial been, and passive-participial written. Their licensing dependencies will be established as the selecting structures are built. The wordless finite T will support tense and agreement without adding another pronounced word.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the nominal objects and the lexical resources for a perfect passive raising construction.

derivationStages.stageRecord: First merge written with the definite nominal, projecting V. This establishes the letter as the Theme of writing in the complement position from which it will later raise. Next merge by with Mary, projecting P; by licenses its nominal complement with oblique Case. The by-phrase is still separate from the predicate, so its connection to the writing event is not yet established.
derivationStages.statement: Build the thematic object position and the by-phrase.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the by-phrase as a right-hand adjunct to the V projection, then merge passive been with that enlarged predicate. Passive Voice licenses the by-phrase as the expression of the writing event's Agent, connecting Mary to written rather than to seems. This passive Voice introduces no external subject DP and supplies no structural accusative Case to the Theme. The letter therefore remains available for subsequent Case licensing. The same Voice head selects the passive-participial form written. This analysis places the passive auxiliary in Voice and does not posit a separate silent external argument or an additional passive auxiliary head.
derivationStages.statement: Construct passive Voice and license Mary as the writer.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge have with the passive Voice projection, establishing perfect selection of the participial auxiliary been. Next merge infinitival to with that perfect projection, licensing the bare form have. These successive selections derive the auxiliary order to have been written without auxiliary movement or an additional realization operation. Nonfinite T has a subject-edge requirement but cannot value the letter's Case; its subject position has not yet been filled.
derivationStages.statement: Build the perfect infinitival clause before subject raising.

values.rule: pronounce the highest occurrence of the nominal chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge the Theme nominal from the complement of written at the edge of the nonfinite T projection. The source position is present in the preceding workspace. This A-movement satisfies nonfinite T's subject-edge requirement but does not value Case. Passive Voice is treated as nonphasal here, so no intervening Voice-edge movement is required. Retain a full, unpronounced lower copy in the object position and pronounce the newly highest occurrence. No PRO is introduced: the infinitival subject and the Theme are occurrences of the same nominal object.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the letter to the embedded subject position.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge seems with the nonfinite T projection, then merge finite T above the resulting V projection. Seems selects a nonfinite propositional complement but assigns no external theta-role, so the letter receives no new thematic interpretation in the matrix clause. No thematic matrix v layer is introduced. Finite T then probes the accessible, Case-unvalued nominal at the embedded subject edge. The embedded nonfinite domain is defective for Case and does not block this dependency. Agree values nominative Case on the nominal chain and third-person singular agreement on finite T. Finally, finite T licenses the present-tense form seems in situ; this analysis uses the supplied inflected lexical form rather than overt V-to-T movement or a separate pronounced suffix. The matrix subject-edge requirement remains to be satisfied.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix raising predicate and establish finite agreement.

values.rule: pronounce only the highest occurrence of the nominal chain

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge the embedded subject nominal at the matrix T edge, using the occurrence already present in the preceding workspace. This satisfies finite T's remaining subject requirement and extends the A-chain whose thematic source is the complement of written. The landing occurrence inherits the chain's nominative licensing; it receives no theta-role from seems. Make the embedded subject copy unpronounced while retaining both it and the already silent object copy. Pronounce only the matrix nominal occurrence. The completed root T projection consequently spells The letter seems to have been written by Mary. Its interpretation combines matrix seeming with a perfect passive writing event: the letter is the Theme, and Mary is the Agent.
derivationStages.statement: Complete matrix subject raising and the surface sentence.

cases.description: Long Swedish V2 clause with a subject relative and an object relative, each with its own operator chain, plus V-to-I-to-C.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night4-20261019/18-sv-long-v2, analysis 1 of 2. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night4-20261019/runs/18-sv-long-v2.
cases.sentence: Igår läste studenten som hade kommit från Uppsala den bok som professorn hade rekommenderat.

relations.relation: theta assignment in the subject relative

values.interpretation: The relative operator denotes the participant who came; Uppsala is the source of that coming.

relations.relation: theta assignment in the object relative

values.interpretation: Igår restricts the matrix reading event to yesterday.

derivationStages.stageRecord: This analysis takes the sentence to mean that yesterday the student who had come from Uppsala read the book that the professor had recommended. The source PP is the optional directional complement of kommit, not a modifier of studenten. A traditional GB architecture is used: subjects originate in Spec-IP, objects originate as complements of V, and relative clauses contain silent operators distinct from the overt relative complementizer som. All projections and lexical selections are assembled here without movement. The inflected nouns studenten and professorn are lexical N terminals under silent definite D heads; den is the overt determiner of bok. The form den bok is retained exactly, without adding a nominal definiteness suffix. First, the determiners establish the nominal specifications shown. Next, kommit assigns its participant role to the subject relative operator and its source role to the PP; från assigns its ground role to Uppsala. Rekommenderat assigns its external role to professorn and its internal role to the object relative operator. Each finite hade selects a participial VP and establishes an embedded past-perfect configuration. Embedded finite auxiliaries remain in V; the silent finite I heads license tense and nominative Case without requiring embedded V-to-I movement. Läste assigns the matrix agent role to studenten and the theme role to den bok. The three finite I heads license nominative Case on their subjects, the transitive verbs license accusative Case on their objects, and från licenses its nominal complement. Finally, Igår is introduced as a matrix VP adjunct, providing the temporal restriction on the reading event. The empty matrix C is reserved for the declarative V2 derivation. The relative operators have not yet moved, and neither finite-verb movement nor temporal topicalization has occurred.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the base structure with från Uppsala inside the subject relative clause.

relations.relation: subject relative A-bar chain and trace licensing

values.dependency: Spec-IP to Spec-CP; nominative subject trace; antecedent-government

values.interpretation: the student who had come from Uppsala

relations.relation: object relative A-bar chain and trace licensing

values.dependency: V-complement to Spec-CP; accusative object trace; lexical government

values.interpretation: the book that the professor had recommended

derivationStages.stageRecord: First, the silent subject operator moves from the previously represented Spec-IP position to Spec-CP of the studenten relative, leaving a nominative subject trace. The operator antecedent-governs that trace through the licensed relative configuration headed by som; no extraction out of the nominal relative island occurs. The resulting CP predicates the property of having come from Uppsala of studenten. Independently, the object operator moves from the complement position of rekommenderat to Spec-CP of the bok relative. Its accusative trace remains lexically governed by rekommenderat. That CP predicates the property of having been recommended by the professor of bok. In both chains the lower position preserves the theta role and Case established earlier. Som remains in C and is not itself the moved nominal. Both relative clauses receive the integrated, restrictive interpretation supported by their nominal attachments.
derivationStages.statement: Form the subject and object relative-operator chains.

values.dependency: successive-cyclic head movement through the nearest inflectional head

derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix V läste moves from its established V position and adjoins to the finite I head. A silent V trace remains beside the object DP, preserving the original thematic and accusative-governing position through the verbal chain. The existing past inflection is represented as the silent inner I of the resulting complex head; läste remains the single lexical word, so this step does not introduce a separate pronounced tense morpheme. This is the intermediate head position required by the chosen successive-cyclic V-to-I-to-C implementation of matrix V2. It is not a claim that Swedish embedded lexical verbs generally raise to I. Neither the matrix subject nor Igår moves at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Move the matrix finite verb through I.

values.interpretation: Yesterday scopes over the matrix reading event.

values.surfaceOrder: Igår — läste — studenten som hade kommit från Uppsala — den bok som professorn hade rekommenderat

derivationStages.stageRecord: First, the complex finite I containing läste moves from its previously established position to matrix C, leaving an I trace. The head chain therefore passes through I rather than skipping it. The subject remains in Spec-IP: its position after the pronounced verb is the consequence of movement of the verb to C, not subject inversion by a separate subject movement. Next, Igår moves from the previously represented VP-adjoined position to Spec-CP and leaves an adverbial trace. Its lower position supplies the interpretation as a temporal modifier of the matrix event, while its higher position supplies the initial topic. The temporal chain is locally contained in the matrix clause and does not extract from either relative-clause island. The final structure has one preverbal constituent, Igår, followed by the finite verb in C, the full subject DP, and the object DP. The PP remains inside the subject relative as the source of coming. The silent chains preserve the previously assigned theta roles and Case, and the overt terminals yield the exact input order.
derivationStages.statement: Complete matrix V2 and temporal topicalization.

cases.description: Irish VSO derived by V-to-I over a VP-internal subject.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/18-ga-vso, analysis 1 of 1. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/18-ga-vso.

relations.relation: Complement selection and internal theta-role assignment

derivationStages.stageRecord: The sentence is analyzed as an Irish finite declarative meaning ‘Seán saw the dog.’ A traditional GB noun-phrase analysis is used: the definite determiner an occupies the specifier of the object NP, and madra heads its N′. The proper name Seán forms a separate NP. The lexical verb Chonaic selects the object NP and assigns it the Theme role; it also governs that NP and assigns objective Case. Chonaic is introduced with its actual, irregular past-tense spelling rather than decomposed into hypothetical concatenative morphemes. Its lexical interpretation is SEE with past inflection. A separate, unpronounced I head bears finite past tense; its connection to the verb will be established when the clause is assembled. The subject has not yet been attached or assigned its external theta role.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the lexical verb, its object, the subject noun phrase, and abstract past tense.

values.configuration: Finite I governs the subject in Spec-VP.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Seán is merged in Spec-VP, where the verbal predicate assigns it the external Experiencer role appropriate to seeing. The resulting VP is the complement of finite I, and I′ projects to IP without an occupied Spec-IP. The past-tense feature of I is identified with the past inflection of Chonaic. Under the Irish government configuration adopted here, finite I governs the VP-internal subject and licenses its nominative Case; the subject therefore need not raise to Spec-IP. This is an explicit commitment to a VP-internal-subject, V-to-I account of Irish VSO order. At this stage the verb is still in its original V position, so the underlying pronounced order inside the assembled clause is subject–verb–object, not yet the input order. IP is taken as the root of this unembedded declarative; no additional C position is required for the analysis.
derivationStages.statement: Build the underlying subject–verb–object clause with a VP-internal subject.

relations.relation: V-to-I head movement and head-chain formation

values.operation: Left-adjoin V to I, leaving a silent V trace.

relations.relation: Proper government of the verbal trace

values.licensingCondition: The raised verbal head properly governs its local head trace.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Chonaic moves from the V position shown in the preceding stage and adjoins to I, forming a complex I head. The moved verb retains its occurrence identity, and a new, silent V trace marks its original position. This local head movement crosses no intervening head and creates a head chain linking the pronounced verb to its theta-assigning and object-Case-assigning position. The trace is properly head-governed by the raised verbal head. The subject remains in Spec-VP with its previously established theta role and nominative Case, while an madra remains the direct object. The resulting order is the verb in I, the VP-internal subject Seán, and the object an madra. The abstract tense head and the verbal trace are silent, so the pronounced terminals yield exactly ‘Chonaic Seán an madra.’ No separate realization mapping is needed because Chonaic was retained throughout as the lexical past form.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the finite verb to I and derive the surface VSO sentence.

cases.description: Japanese ditransitive with case heads: the subject raises to Spec-T and the accusative object scrambles above it.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/01-ja-scrambling, analysis 1 of 1. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/01-ja-scrambling.
cases.sentence: 本をメアリーがジョンに渡した。

derivationStages.stageRecord: External Merge combines 本 with を, メアリー with が, and ジョン with に. Each resulting object is labeled K by its case-particle head; the common noun can itself constitute the nominal complement, while the proper names are referential D items. Labels name the projecting heads rather than introducing independent phrase-level symbols. The accusative and nominative particles have their overt forms, but their structural licensing will be established in the clause. The selected verb is the intact inflected lexical item 渡した. This lexicalist analysis does not decompose its written form into separate pronounced V and T terminals: a silent past T will license its tense. Silent transitive v and declarative C are also selected. All three particles remain overt throughout the derivation.
derivationStages.statement: Select the lexical objects and assemble the three head-final case-marked nominals.

derivationStages.stageRecord: First merge the accusative nominal with 渡した, establishing the book as the transferred theme. Next merge the に-marked nominal at the higher internal-argument position of the same V-labeled structure, establishing John as recipient. With 渡す, this に phrase is an argument of transfer, not a location adjunct or an agent phrase. The analysis implements the two internal arguments directly in the verbal domain rather than adding a separate applicative head. This yields the underlying recipient–theme–verb order from which the pronounced object will later scramble. The dative particle receives its inherent recipient-case licensing here.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the transfer predicate with the book as theme and John as recipient.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge transitive v with the transfer predicate and then merge the が-marked nominal at the edge of the resulting v-labeled object. This introduces Mary as the agent of the handing event. Transitive v licenses structural accusative on the book nominal, whose particle を was already present. The recipient's inherently licensed dative does not compete for this accusative dependency. The subject remains in its external-argument position at this stage, providing the source occurrence for subsequent subject movement.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce Mary as the external argument and license the theme's accusative case.

values.implementation: silent T licenses an intact inflected V; no V-to-T movement

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge silent past T to the right of the v domain. T licenses the past specification of the already selected inflected verb 渡した through the verbal domain. This is a lexicalist licensing dependency, not an operation that changes the verb's spelling or moves it into T; consequently no separate realization association is needed. T then licenses nominative on Mary, the closest structurally eligible nominal. No overt person or number agreement is posited for Japanese. Mary has not yet moved, so both nominative licensing and the following movement can be anchored to her independently visible external-argument occurrence.
derivationStages.statement: Merge past T and establish tense and nominative licensing.

relations.relation: subject Internal Merge and chain pronunciation

values.pronunciation: higher occurrence pronounced; lower occurrence unpronounced

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge takes the previously established Mary nominal from the edge of v and remerges it at the edge of the T-labeled object. This analysis adopts a subject-edge requirement on finite T; it does not derive subject raising from overt agreement morphology. The two occurrences form an A-chain. The higher occurrence is pronounced and the lower occurrence, including its name and case particle, is unpronounced. The lower occurrence retains the external theta-role position established earlier, while nominative licensing remains the dependency already established with T. The resulting pronounced order before object scrambling is Mary–John–book–handed.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the subject to the finite clause edge.

values.interpretiveDependency: the fronted nominal remains the theme through its lower occurrence
values.landingPosition: outer T edge above the subject
values.pronunciation: higher occurrence pronounced; lower occurrence unpronounced

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internal Merge takes the book nominal from its previously displayed position beside V and remerges it at an outer edge of the T-labeled clause, above the raised subject. This is clause-internal object scrambling: the moved constituent includes を, and no separate topic head or resumptive pronoun is introduced. The higher object occurrence is pronounced; the complete lower occurrence is unpronounced but preserves the selected theme position and the accusative dependency. The movement adds no new theta-role. Finally merge silent declarative C with the scrambled clause. All heads are ordered consistently with the head-final implementation, and no verb movement is required. Reading the pronounced terminals yields exactly 本をメアリーがジョンに渡した, with the sentence-final punctuation supplied by the written input.
derivationStages.statement: Scramble the accusative object above the subject and complete the declarative clause.

cases.description: German middle-field scrambling of the object across a quantified nominative subject in a head-final IP.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/38-de-scrambling.r2, analysis 1 of 2. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/38-de-scrambling.r2.
cases.sentence: dass das Buch niemand gelesen hat

relations.relation: Object selection, theta-role assignment, and Case government

derivationStages.stageRecord: On this reading, the sentence means that nobody has read the book. The participle gelesen selects das Buch as its Theme and assigns it accusative Case under government. The neuter determiner das does not distinguish accusative from nominative, so the surface form alone does not establish this assignment. The object precedes the verbal head in the head-final V′. Niemand is prepared as the external argument, while finite hat and the complementizer dass remain separate. This analysis uses NP with a determiner specifier, a subject base-generated in Spec-IP, and a perfect auxiliary base-generated in I; it therefore does not require subject raising or auxiliary movement.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the transitive predicate with das Buch as its underlying object.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The VP combines with head-final I to form I′, and niemand occupies Spec-IP. First, predication connects niemand to the VP's external Agent role. Finite hat then licenses nominative Case on that subject and agrees with its third-person singular features. Finally, the auxiliary selects the participial VP and establishes the perfect construction. These commitments yield the underlying order niemand das Buch gelesen hat. The finite auxiliary remains in I: the difference between the participle and auxiliary positions is represented directly, rather than derived by an unrecorded movement.
derivationStages.statement: Build the underlying subject–object–participle–auxiliary IP.

values.dependency: the landing NP c-commands and binds its trace; the verb governs the trace
values.interpretation: reconstruction to the object position is available

derivationStages.stageRecord: Das Buch moves from the complement position already present inside V′ to a left-adjoined IP position. The landing occurrence retains the object's identity, and an unpronounced NP trace replaces it at the source. This local A′-scrambling places the object before niemand without making it the subject. The resulting chain connects the pronounced NP to its original Theme and accusative position: gelesen governs the trace, and the landing NP c-commands and binds it. The trace thus meets the relevant government requirement. Reconstruction to the object position remains available; the definite object does not require a separate analysis merely for that option.
derivationStages.statement: Scramble the accusative object across the nominative subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The initial complementizer dass selects the finite IP produced by scrambling, forming C′ and CP. C is head-initial, whereas I and V are head-final. Dass occupies C, and this subordinate derivation contains no finite-verb movement to C. Consequently, the overt order is exactly dass das Buch niemand gelesen hat. The scrambled object is adjoined to IP, not placed in Spec-CP. The result is a complete subordinate CP; the input provides no matrix predicate, so none is supplied. These records complete the overt derivation without adding a distinct covert scope reading.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the dass-clause with an object–subject middle field.

cases.description: Object control of PRO inside a VP shell where the verb raises above its object.
cases.source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character-spellout-v3 contract, commit bcf1b56, night3-20261019/53-en-object-control, analysis 1 of 1. Exact copy; tokens are the run's shared word list. Saved in ~/Library/Application Support/Babel/codex-qualification/night3-20261019/runs/53-en-object-control.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the intransitive verb leave with a silent verbalizing head, then externally merge PRO as the embedded external argument. The thematic relation identifies PRO as the participant who leaves. This analysis treats leave as an agentive intransitive predicate, with no syntactically represented object. Projection labels name the projecting heads in Bare Phrase Structure; they do not introduce independent bar-level primitives. PRO is intrinsically unpronounced, independently of any later movement.
derivationStages.statement: Build the embedded predicate with its thematic null subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge infinitival T, pronounced to, with the embedded verbal structure. T selects the nonfinite predicate and licenses its bare verbal form. Under the null-Case implementation adopted here, infinitival T also licenses PRO in its thematic position. These dependencies are established before PRO raises to the embedded subject position.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce infinitival to and license the embedded null subject.

values.pronunciation: both PRO occurrences are intrinsically silent

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge PRO from the already represented embedded external-argument position at the edge of the T projection. This satisfies the subject-edge requirement of infinitival T without assigning another thematic role. The lower occurrence retains its identity, and the new higher occurrence shares its lineage. Both occurrences remain silent because the moving subject is PRO.
derivationStages.statement: Raise PRO to the embedded subject position.

values.interpretation: John is the understood subject of leave

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent infinitival C with the embedded T projection. Merge persuaded with that clause, then merge John at the edge of the resulting V projection. This binary structure distinguishes the individual persuaded from the clausal content of the persuasion: John is the affected addressee, and the infinitival clause supplies the intended action. John asymmetrically c-commands the embedded subject and obligatorily controls PRO. Thus John is independently a matrix thematic argument, not an embedded subject raised into the matrix clause. The verb enters as the lexically inflected form persuaded; its past-tense feature will be checked against matrix T.
derivationStages.statement: Build the persuasion predicate and establish object control.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge transitive v with the matrix V projection. The new head probes its complement and agrees with John, the accessible nominal at the edge of that projection, valuing John's structural Case as accusative. John remains in its thematic position; no object movement is required. The higher verbal head also supplies the landing site for the subsequent verb movement.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce transitive v and license the matrix object.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move persuaded from its previously represented V position and adjoin it to matrix v. The landing occurrence is pronounced, and the lower occurrence becomes silent. The resulting head precedes the V projection containing John, producing the surface verb–object order despite John's position at the edge of that lower projection. This is V-to-v head movement, not movement of John or movement of the infinitival clause.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the matrix verb above its object.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Externally merge Mary at the edge of the matrix v projection. Matrix v assigns Mary the external thematic role of agent of persuasion. Mary is therefore distinct from both John, the individual persuaded, and PRO, the understood subject of leaving. The embedded subject remains controlled by John rather than by Mary.
derivationStages.statement: Merge Mary as the persuader.

values.morphologicalImplementation: checking of a lexically inflected verb

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge silent finite T with the matrix verbal structure. T agrees with Mary, the highest accessible nominal, and values her Case as nominative while obtaining third-person singular agreement. T then checks the past-tense specification of the already inflected verb persuaded in v. This adopts lexicalist feature checking: the written verb is present from its introduction, no new morphological exponent is added here, and no V-to-T movement is assumed. Consequently, the ordinary pronounced terminals require no special realization association.

Such then merges at the edge of that determiner-headed object, contributing a contextually salient degree or kind of mess. This treats such as a predeterminer, rather than as an adjective inside the nominal restriction. The remaining objects are available separately: participial seen, an unpronounced agent-introducing light verb, I, negative temporal Never, finite perfect have, and an unpronounced declarative complementizer. Finite perfect have then merges above that structure, selecting the participial predicate and locating its experiential interval relative to the present. T probes its complement and agrees with the first-person singular subject I, licensing nominative case while the subject remains in its original position. The subject has not yet satisfied T's edge requirement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The silent declarative complementizer merges with TP. Its negative-inversion specification requires a negative expression at its edge and an overt finite head in its head domain; the negative-edge requirement remains outstanding here. Have then moves from the T position already present in the preceding workspace and adjoins to C. The upper auxiliary occurrence is pronounced and the lower T occurrence is silenced. Because the subject has already raised to the TP edge, the resulting order is have before I. This is inversion within a declarative negative-fronting construction, not an interrogative clause.

The higher occurrence is pronounced and the lower occurrence is silenced, while the lower occurrence preserves the temporal modification relation established before movement. The fronted negative expression satisfies C's outstanding negative-edge requirement and licenses the already established auxiliary inversion.
